info.title: ballchasing.com API
info.summary: Upload, search and read Rocket League replays and replay groups.
info.description:
This is the [ballchasing.com](https://ballchasing.com) API documentation.

## Authentication

All API calls **must** be authenticated using an API token,
[which can be retrieved/generated here](https://ballchasing.com/upload).

To authenticate an API call, pass the API token, as is, as the value of the `Authorization` header
(there is **no** `Bearer` prefix):

```http
Authorization: $token
```

For example, using curl:

```bash
curl 'https://ballchasing.com/api/' \
  -H "Authorization: $token"
```

The upload endpoint also accepts a **group upload token** (it starts with `g/`): the uploaded replays then go
to that group, owned by the group's owner. A group's owner gets its token from the group's page on the site, or
with [`GET`/`POST /groups/{id}/token`](#tag/groups/get-group-upload-token). The other endpoints only accept
API keys.

A missing key gets a `401` with `"error": "missing API key"`, an unknown one a `401` with
`"error": "invalid API key"`.

## Rate limiting

Many of the APIs are rate limited to avoid abuse and buggy clients hogging all the server resources.
The limits depend on your [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/ballchasing) tier:

| Tier | Typical limits (most endpoints) |
|------|---------------------------------|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls/second |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls/second |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls/second, 2000 to 5000/hour |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls/second, 1000 to 2000/hour |
| All others | 2 calls/second, 500 to 1000/hour |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls/second |
| Organisation and bot accounts (approved by hand) | 16 calls/second |

Each endpoint documents its exact limits in a **Rate limits** table (and, for tools, in the
`x-rate-limits` extension of the operation in the [OpenAPI document](https://ballchasing.com/doc/api/openapi.json)). The limits are counted per
account (all its API keys together) and per endpoint. An account matching several rows gets the first one of
the endpoint's table among the patron tiers, Discord moderators and approved accounts (in this order: Legend,
GC, Champion, Discord moderator, organisation, bot, Diamond, Gold).

When you hit a rate limit, the server responds with a `429` status code, in which case your client
should cool down before retrying: the `Retry-After` header holds the number of seconds to wait (rounded down:
`0` means retry within the second). The body is the usual error object, with `"error": "Too many requests"`.

Downloading replay files has, in addition, a **daily limit on the files uploaded by other people**: see
[Download a replay file](#tag/replays/download-replay-file).

## Errors

Errors are JSON objects with an `error` message, plus a random Rocket League quick chat (`chat`), and the
`request_id` and `server` to quote when reporting a problem:

```json
{
  "error": "not found",
  "chat": {"Poncho": "Whew.", "YOU": "Oops"},
  "request_id": "5A56088B:A9C6_A2379E0D:01BB_6AFFDAAC_2F2FA0:1E0D5E",
  "server": "hzprod-front-1"
}
```

A few answers are lighter: the `409` (duplicate) and `429` (upload quota) of the upload endpoint have no
`request_id` nor `server`, and a request body over 32 KiB on the endpoints other than the upload is refused with
a `413` and the plain text body `request too large`.

An unknown path gets a `404` (`"error": "not found"`), a known path with another method a `405`
(`"error": "method not allowed"`). Query parameters, path parameters and JSON strings must be valid UTF-8
without NUL characters (`400` otherwise).

tags.name: ping
tags.description: Check that your API key works and that the API is reachable.

tags.name: upload
tags.description:
Upload replay files.

The upload endpoint accepts both a personal API key and a **group upload token** (`g/...`).

tags.name: replays
tags.description:
Search, read, update and delete replays, and download their original files.

> **Warning**
> The try-it console sends **real** requests with your key: `PATCH` and `DELETE` change or delete your
> replays for good, and downloads of other people's files count toward your daily quota.

tags.name: groups
tags.description:
Replay groups allow you to group multiple replays in a tree like structure, to organise them and to get
access to multi-game stats.

> **Warning**
> The try-it console sends **real** requests with your key: `PATCH` and `DELETE` change or delete your
> groups for good, and `POST /groups/{id}/token` replaces the group's upload token.

get.description:
Use this API to:

* check if your API key is correct
* check if the ballchasing API is reachable
* get the upload quota of your account
* get how many original replay files of other accounts your account downloaded today, and its daily limit
  (`quota.replay_file_downloads`), before starting a batch of downloads

**Rate limits**: Not rate limited.

post.description:
Upload a replay file to ballchasing.com, as a single part named `file` of a `multipart/form-data` body.

Returns `201` on success (with the id of the created replay), or `409` for a duplicate replay (with the id of
the existing replay).

With a **group upload token** (`Authorization: g/...`), the replay goes to the token's group. The `409` for a
replay that the group's owner already has **outside** that group (and its sub-groups) has no `id` nor
`location`: only `error` and `chat`. It still tells that the owner already has the file, which the uploader
holds anyway (by design: storing a second copy or answering `201` with a made-up id would break
deduplication).

> **Note**
> The upload quota of your account (replays per day and per week) is in the response of [Ping](#tag/ping).

**Rate limits**: Limited by the account's upload quota (see `quota` in the ping response) rather than per second.

x-rate-limits.note: Limited by the account's upload quota (see `quota` in the ping response) rather than per second.

parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: Visibility of the uploaded replay.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
Id of the group (one of yours) to put the uploaded replay in. With a group upload token, it can only be
the token's group.

file.description:
The `.replay` file: its name must end with `.replay`, and it is at most 50 MiB (52,428,800 bytes).
Only the first part named `file` is read.

title.description:
Optional title of the replay, so that it is named in the same request instead of a
[PATCH](#tag/replays/patch-replay) after the upload. The same rules as that PATCH: at most
1,024 characters, valid UTF-8, no NUL character. A title that breaks them is ignored and the upload
goes on without one (no error). The first text value of `title` is used (a file part named `title`
is ignored); empty means no title. It names a new replay only: a duplicate (`409`) keeps its own
title. Like every field, it counts in the request size limit (see `413`).

match.description:
Optional: the game's match data, as Psyonix's match history API returns it for this game (an RLAPI
`Match` object), sent as a JSON text field. It lets ballchasing show each player's MMR before and
after the match. Only the fields listed here are read; others are allowed and ignored. Without
`MatchGUID`, the rest is not used.

The values are reports: ballchasing checks them against its own readings from Psyonix before
showing any of them, and hides those that disagree.

Limits: at most 64 KiB, nested at most 32 levels deep, at most 64 `Players`. A value that breaks
them, is not a JSON object, or has a field of the wrong type is ignored: the upload goes on and its
response is the same as without `match`. The first text value of `match` is used; a file part named
`match` is ignored.

x-codeSamples.label: Python (requests, with duplicates)
x-codeSamples.source:
import requests

upload_url = "https://ballchasing.com/api/v2/upload?visibility=public"

def upload(path, token):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        r = requests.post(upload_url, headers={"Authorization": token}, files={"file": f})

    if r.status_code == 201:
        # replay successfully created, return its id
        return r.json()["id"]
    elif r.status_code == 409:  # duplicate replay
        # either raise an error, or return the existing replay id
        # (absent for a group upload token when the existing replay is outside the token's group)
        return r.json().get("id")
    else:
        # raise an error for other status codes (50x, ...)
        r.raise_for_status()

Location.description: The new replay's page on ballchasing.com.

Invalid request: not a `multipart/form-data` body, no `file` part, a file name not ending with `.replay`,
a file over 50 MiB, not a valid replay, an invalid `visibility`, a `group` that is not one of yours (or
not the group upload token's).

value.error: cannot override group in a call made using group upload token

groupTokenElsewhere.summary: Group token, the owner has the replay outside the group

get.description:
Filter and retrieve replays, most recent uploads first by default.

You get the public replays, and your own whatever their visibility. With `group` set to a shared group, the
group's owner's replays in it are listed whatever their visibility too.

## Pagination

A page holds at most `count` replays (default 50, max 200). When there are more, the response has a `next`
field: the **full URL** of the next page, with the same filters and an opaque `after` cursor. Call it as is,
with your `Authorization` header, until a response has no `next`:

```python
url = "https://ballchasing.com/api/replays?player-id=steam:76561198141161044&count=200"
while url:
    page = requests.get(url, headers={"Authorization": token}).json()
    for replay in page["list"]:
        ...
    url = page.get("next")
```

`count` is the total number of replays matching the filters (all pages), counted up to 10,000.

## Repeated parameters

`playlist` can be repeated to match **any** of the values: `?playlist=ranked-duels&playlist=ranked-doubles`.

`player-name` and `player-id` can be repeated to find the replays with **all** of these players:
`?player-id=steam:1&player-id=steam:2`. The number of players in one search depends on your account:

| Tier | Players per search |
|------|-------------------:|
| Legend patrons | 10 |
| GC and Champion patrons | 6 |
| Diamond patrons | 4 |
| Gold patrons | 3 |
| All others | 2 |
| Discord moderators | 6 |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 10 |

More players get a `400` (`"you can search for up to 2 players"`).

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 2000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 500 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Filter replays by title.

parameters.name: player-name
parameters.description:
Filter replays by a player's name. Repeat it to find the replays with all of these players:
`?player-name=name1&player-name=name2`.

A name matches the players whose name contains it (as words or a word prefix, case insensitive); quote it
(`"Can't Fly"`, quotes included) for the players with exactly this name. A value starting with a platform
prefix (`steam:`, `epic:`, `ps4:`, `xbox:`, `switch:`, `psynet:`) makes every `player-name` value a
player id, as with `player-id`.

parameters.name: player-id
parameters.description:
Filter replays by a player's platform id, as `$platform:$id`, e.g. `steam:76561198141161044`,
`ps4:gamertag` (case insensitive). Repeat it to find the replays with all of these players:
`?player-id=steam:1&player-id=steam:2`. With `player-id` values, the `player-name` ones are ignored.

parameters.name: playlist
parameters.description:
Filter replays by one or more playlists (any of them). Prefix a value with `!` to **exclude** that
playlist instead (e.g. `!private`; not offered by the dropdown).

parameters.name: season
parameters.description:
Filter replays by season: a number between 1 and 14 for the old seasons, or `f1`, `f2`, ... for the free
to play seasons.

parameters.name: match-result
parameters.description:
Filter **your** replays by result: the replays where the API key's owner (by Steam id) played and won, or
lost.

parameters.name: min-rank
parameters.description:
Only include replays whose lowest ranked player is at least this rank. `grand-champion` is the same as
`grand-champion-1`.

parameters.name: max-rank
parameters.description: Only include replays whose highest ranked player is at most this rank (any division of it).

parameters.name: pro
parameters.description: Only include replays containing at least one pro player.

parameters.name: uploader
parameters.description:
Only include replays uploaded by this user: a SteamID64 (`76561198141161044`), or the special value
`me` for your own replays. `is:player` keeps the replays whose uploader is one of their players,
`!is:player` the others.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
Only include replays directly under this group (not the replays of its child groups). With a shared
group, its owner's replays are included whatever their visibility.

parameters.name: map
parameters.description:
Only include replays played on this map: a map code of [`GET /maps`](#tag/misc/list-maps) (`400` for an
unknown one).

parameters.name: created-before
parameters.description: Only include replays uploaded at or before this date (RFC 3339, e.g. `2020-01-02T15:00:05+01:00`).

parameters.name: created-after
parameters.description: Only include replays uploaded at or after this date (RFC 3339, e.g. `2020-01-02T15:00:05+01:00`).

parameters.name: replay-date-before
parameters.description: Only include games played at or before this date (RFC 3339, e.g. `2020-01-02T15:00:05+01:00`).

parameters.name: replay-date-after
parameters.description: Only include games played at or after this date (RFC 3339, e.g. `2020-01-02T15:00:05+01:00`).

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Replays per page.

parameters.name: sort-by
parameters.description: Sort field: `created` (upload date) or `replay-date` (when the game was played).

parameters.name: sort-dir
parameters.description: Sort direction.

parameters.name: roulette
parameters.description:
`true`: return **one** random replay among the matching ones (`count` is then 1, or absent when none
matches), with no `next` page.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Pagination cursor. Do not build it: it is part of the `next` URL of the previous page.

page.summary: A page with a next page

400.description: Invalid parameter (`error` tells which), or more players than your account may search at once.

value.error: invalid "sort-by"="upload-date": must be one of replay-date, created
you can search for up to 2 players

503.description: The search timed out or was incomplete (no partial page is returned): retry later.

get.description:
Retrieve a replay's details and stats.

The response depends on the replay's `status`: a processed replay (`ok`) has all its stats; a replay that is
not processed yet (`pending`) or could not be processed (`failed`) only has its metadata.

Players and teams stats also have:

* `core`: `epic_saves`, `clears`, `centers`, `aerial_hits`, `first_touches`, `flip_resets`, `crossbar_hits`,
  `bicycle_hits` and `juggle_hits`, counted by Rocket League itself and read as is from the replay file
  (`flip_resets` in particular isn't verified by ballchasing)
* `demo`: `inflicted_in_defensive_half`, `inflicted_in_offensive_half`, `taken_in_defensive_half` and
  `taken_in_offensive_half`, based on the attacker's position

These fields are **omitted** when the replay doesn't track them, and `0` when it does but the value is zero.
The `core` counters are only tracked by replays from Rocket League's September 2026 update onwards. The demos
split by field half are available for any replay processed since October 2026; replays processed before that
get them once reprocessed.

`play_duration` is the time actually played, in seconds, without the kickoff countdowns (omitted for replays
processed before it was computed).

You can read the public and unlisted replays, and your own. A private replay of someone else gets a `404`,
unless you pass a shared group holding it (`group`).

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
Id of a shared group holding the replay: its owner's replays in it can then be read whatever their
visibility, as on the group's page.

ok.summary: A processed replay (one player per team shown)

failed.summary: A replay that could not be processed

patch.description:
Change one or more fields of one of your replays: title, visibility, group. The changes are applied together,
or not at all. An empty object changes nothing (`204`).

`group` only changes **your** groups: it can also put a replay of someone else that you can see (public or
unlisted) in one of your groups, or take it out of them. `title` and `visibility` need the replay to be yours
(`404` otherwise).

> **Warning**
> This changes the replay for good. The try-it console sends a **real** request with your key.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

400.description:
Invalid request: invalid JSON or visibility, a title over 1024 characters, or a replay you cannot see (when
setting `group`).

example.error: invalid replay visibility 'hidden': must be one of 'private', 'public', 'unlisted'

404.description: No such replay (or not yours, for `title` and `visibility`), or no such group of yours.

value.error: error moving replay 7fd09c82-b0d8-4d85-b875-fe1dd3a3a3c1 to group rlcs-s6-day1-xxd: not found

delete.description:
Delete one of your replays.

> **Warning**
> This is permanent and cannot be undone. The try-it console sends a **real** request with your key.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |

| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |

get.description:
Download the original `.replay` file of a replay.

Serving largish (binary) files like replays is costly (server CPU and I/O time, object storage access costs,
network egress costs), which is why this endpoint has lower rate limits than usual.

> **Warning**
> **Daily limit on other people's replay files.** On top of the rate limits, each account (all its API keys
> together) can only download a limited number of original replay files **uploaded by other people** per
> day. Trying this endpoint here on someone else's replay counts toward that limit.

| Tier | Other people's files per day |
|------|-----------------------------:|
| Legend patrons | 2500 |
| GC patrons | 1000 |
| Champion patrons | 500 |
| Diamond patrons | 250 |
| Gold patrons | 100 |
| All others | 50 |
| Discord moderators | 500 |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 2500 |

Discord moderators and approved organisation and bot accounts get the larger of their row and their tier's.

Patrons whose current pledge started before 15 November 2026 (UTC), with their Patreon account connected, get
twice their tier's limit while their pledge continues (up to the tier they had when this perk launched): a
goodwill gesture that may be revoked at the site owner's discretion, and not given to accounts collecting
other players' replays in bulk.

**Your own files are not limited**: the replays you uploaded, including those uploaded with one of your group
upload tokens. A replay of someone else counts even when it is in one of your groups.

The limit is shared with the site: the files downloaded on ballchasing.com and through the API count together.

A day is a calendar day in UTC: the count restarts at 00:00 UTC. Distinct replays are counted: downloading the
same replay again on the same day does not count twice, and a download that fails because the server could
not read the file does not count (one that you interrupt does).

Once the limit is reached, the server responds with a `429` to any other replay of someone else until the
next day (the replays already counted that day can still be downloaded). The `Retry-After` header holds the
number of seconds until the count restarts, and the body has `limit`, `count` and `reset` fields, which tell
this limit apart from the rate limits.

To know where an account stands before starting a batch of downloads, [Ping](#tag/ping) answers the day's count
and the limit in `quota.replay_file_downloads` (`used`, `max`, `resets_at`); pinging does not count.

The replay stats and metadata (`GET /replays/{id}`) are not concerned by this limit.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 2 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| Diamond patrons | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 400 calls |
| All others | 1 calls | 200 calls |
| Discord moderators | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 2 calls | - |

x-daily-quota.scope: other people's original replay files, per account and UTC day

Content-Length.description: Size of the file, in bytes.

410.description:
The replay exists but its file is lost: the server no longer has it (a stored copy that went missing or bad,
or a replay whose upload never stored it). It does not count toward the daily limit. It will not come back by
trying again.

example.error: the file of this replay is lost

429.description:
Rate limit reached (the body is a plain error), or **daily limit on other people's files** reached (the
body also has `limit`, `count` and `reset`). Either way, wait `Retry-After` seconds.

dailyLimit.summary: Daily limit on other people's files

value.error: daily limit reached: your account can download 50 original replay files uploaded by other people per day (UTC), on the site and through the API together. It resets at 2026-11-17T00:00:00Z. Replays you uploaded are not limited. Daily limits per account type: https://ballchasing.com/doc/using-the-site#downloads

get.description:
Filter and retrieve replay groups, most recently created first by default.

Without `group`, only **top level** groups are listed; with `group`, only the direct children of that group.
You get your own groups, and the other people's groups that hold at least one replay you can see (public), or
that are shared. Add `creator=me` to only get yours.

## Pagination

A page holds at most `count` groups (default 50, max 200). When there are more, the response has a `next`
field: the **full URL** of the next page, with the same filters and an opaque `after` cursor. Call it as is,
with your `Authorization` header, until a response has no `next`. Unlike `GET /replays`, the response has no
total `count`.

`GET /groups` and `POST /groups` share their rate limit counters.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 2000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 500 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

Only include the direct children of this group (not their own sub-groups). Without it, only the top level

post.description:
Create a new replay group, at the top level or as a child of one of your groups.

Group names are unique among the groups of the same parent (of yours), and trees are 32 levels deep at most.

`GET /groups` and `POST /groups` share their rate limit counters.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

Location.description: API URL of the new group.

400.description:
Invalid request: invalid JSON, name (missing, shorter than 3 or longer than 255 bytes) or identification,
duplicate name, no such parent (or not yours), too deep (32 levels at most), or too many groups (100,000 per
account).

get.description:
Retrieve a replay group's info and the stats of its players and teams.

Players and teams `cumulative` and `game_average` stats also have:

* `core`: `epic_saves`, `clears`, `centers`, `aerial_hits`, `first_touches`, `flip_resets`, `crossbar_hits`,
  `bicycle_hits` and `juggle_hits`, counted by Rocket League itself and read as is from the replay file
  (`flip_resets` in particular isn't verified by ballchasing)
* `demo`: `inflicted_in_defensive_half`, `inflicted_in_offensive_half`, `taken_in_defensive_half` and
  `taken_in_offensive_half`, based on the attacker's position

These fields are **omitted** when none of the group's games track them. Otherwise, `cumulative` is the total
over the games that track them, and `game_average` is averaged over those games only, so groups mixing old and
new replays average correctly.

### Replays of the same game

Several players often upload their own replay of the same game. Each group has a `dedup` setting (`true` for
groups created since November 2026, `false` for older ones until their owner changes it):

* `true`: the stats count each game once, from one of its replays (the longest in-game duration, then the
  earliest upload). Games, wins, totals and averages ignore the other replays of that game.
* `false`: every replay counts, as before.

Add `dedup=on` or `dedup=off` to choose for one request, whatever the group's setting: a tool reading groups
owned by others can count the same way across all of them.

The `duplicates` counts say how many of the group's replays are the same game (the same with `on` and `off`).
Which replays they are: `GET /groups/{id}/duplicate-replays`.

Two replays are the same game when they share the match id, the server's match start time (written in replays
since September 2024), the score, the duration (within 3 seconds) and enough of the same players on the same
sides. Older replays are never merged.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

parameters.name: dedup
parameters.description:
Count each game once (`on`) or every replay (`off`) for this request. Without it, the group's `dedup` setting
decides. `true` and `false` work too.

ok.summary: A group with stats (one player shown)

pending.summary: A group with replays not processed yet

patch.description:
Change one or more fields of one of your groups: player and team identification, parent, sharing, and the
replays directly in it. The changes are applied together, or not at all.

> **Warning**
> This changes the group for good. The try-it console sends a **real** request with your key.

Someone else's group gets a `404`, like an unknown one.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

topLevel.summary: Make it a top level group

unassign.summary: Take replays out of your groups

400.description:
Invalid request: invalid JSON or identification, more than 150 replays to assign or 300 to unassign, an
invalid or inaccessible replay id, or a parent that does not exist (or is not yours), is the group itself or
one of its sub-groups, or would make the tree deeper than 32 levels.

example.error: error while changing group parent to "new-parent-group-id": not found

404.description: No such group, or not yours.

delete.description:
Delete one of your groups, with its sub-groups and their upload tokens. The replays are **not** deleted: they
just leave the deleted groups.

> **Warning**
> This is permanent and cannot be undone. The try-it console sends a **real** request with your key.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

409.description: The group holds a group of another user, so it cannot be deleted.

example.error: This group holds a group of another user: it cannot be deleted

get.description:
The group's replays that hold a game already held in another of its replays: one row per replay **not counted**
when the group counts each game once (see "Replays of the same game" in `GET /groups/{id}`), with the replay that
counts (`same_game_as`).

A game held in 3 replays gives 2 rows with the same `same_game_as`. The replay that counts and the games held in a
single replay have no row. The rows over all pages add up to the group's `duplicates.duplicate_replays`. The list
is the same whatever the group's `dedup` setting, and only uses the replays you may see.

Rows are sorted by `replay_id`. When there are more, the response has a `next` field: the **full URL** of the
next page. Each page is computed again from the group's current replays: if replays are added or removed while
you walk the pages, a page can reflect the change.

**Rate limits**

| Tier | Per second | Per hour |
|------|-----------:|---------:|
| Legend and GC patrons | 16 calls | - |
| Champion patrons | 8 calls | - |
| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |
| All others | 2 calls | 1000 calls |
| Discord moderators | 8 calls | - |
| Organisation and bot accounts | 16 calls | - |

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Returns at most `count` rows.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only the rows whose `replay_id` comes after this one. Set by the `next` URL.

422.description: The group holds more replays than its owner's limit for stats, or took too long to compute.

example.error: This group has too many replays to compute its duplicates (the same limit as its stats)

get.description:
Get the **upload token** of one of your groups: a key that uploads replays straight into that group (with
`POST /v2/upload`, as the `Authorization` header), for an auto-upload tool or a teammate. Replays uploaded with
it are **yours**: they count against your upload quota, and as your own files for the daily download limit.

A group has at most one token. `204` when the group has none yet: create it with `POST`.

Group upload tokens are available to Patreon patrons (Gold and up) and to the accounts they were enabled for;
other accounts get a `404`.

**Rate limits**

| Diamond patrons | 4 calls | 5000 calls |
| Gold patrons | 2 calls | 2000 calls |

> **Warning**

apiKey.name: Authorization
apiKey.description:
Your API token, [from the upload page](https://ballchasing.com/upload), sent as is (no `Bearer` prefix).
The upload endpoint also accepts a group upload token (`g/...`).

Chat.description: A random Rocket League quick chat exchange, for fun. Keys are speaker names, values are quick chats.

max.description: Most replays allowed in the window (absent when unlimited).

unlimited.description: `true` when the window has no limit (`max` is then absent).

error.description: Set when the uploads could not be counted (`used` is then 0).

ReplayFileDownloads.description:
Downloads of original replay files uploaded by **other accounts**, today (UTC), against the account's daily limit
(see [Download a replay file](#tag/replays/download-replay-file)). One count for the API (`GET /api/replays/{id}/file`),
the site's download button and group zips together; each replay counts once a day, and the replays the account
uploaded never count. Once `used` reaches `max`, downloading a replay not downloaded yet today answers 429 until
`resets_at`. Reading it (pinging) never changes it.

used.description:
Distinct replays of other accounts downloaded today (UTC). Can be above `max` after the account's tier went
down during the day.

max.description: The account's daily limit (absent when unlimited).

unlimited.description: `true` when the account has no daily limit (`max` is then absent).

resets_at.description: When the count restarts at 0 (the next midnight UTC), RFC 3339.

error.description: Set when the count could not be read (`used` is then 0).

name.description: Steam name of the API key's owner.

steam_id.description: SteamID64 of the API key's owner.

type.description:
The kind of account behind the key, the first that applies: `admin`, `org` (approved organisation
account), `bot` (approved bot account), its Patreon tier (`gold`, `diamond`, `champion`, `gc`, `legend`),
else `regular`.

quota.description:
The quotas of the account: replays uploaded in the last 24 hours and 7 days, and the maximum of each window;
original replay files of other accounts downloaded today (UTC), and the daily limit.

Error.description: The body of every error response.

request_id.description: The id of the request, to quote when reporting a problem.

server.description: The server that answered, to quote when reporting a problem.

Visibility.description:
* `public`: listed and searchable by everyone
* `unlisted`: visible to anyone with the link, not listed
* `private`: only visible to you

UploadMatch.title: Match
UploadMatch.description:
The game's match data, as Psyonix's match history API returns it for this game (an RLAPI `Match` object). Only the
fields below are read; other fields are allowed and ignored. Every field is optional except `MatchGUID`: without it,
the rest is not used.

The values are reports: ballchasing checks them against its own readings from Psyonix before showing any of them,
and hides those that disagree.

Limits: at most 64 KiB, nested at most 32 levels deep, at most 64 `Players`. A value that breaks them, is not a
JSON object, or has a field of the wrong type is ignored: the upload goes on and its response is the same as
without `match`.

MatchGUID.description: The game's match GUID. It ties the report to the replay; the same GUID is read from the replay file.

Playlist.description: Psyonix's playlist id (e.g. `10` ranked duel, `11` ranked doubles, `13` ranked standard).

RecordStartTimestamp.description: Start of the match, Unix time in seconds.

PlayerID.description: Platform, platform id and split-screen index, separated by `|`.

Skills.title: MatchPlayerSkills
Skills.description: The player's skill in this match's playlist, before (`Prev*`) and after the match.

Mu.description: Skill after the match, on Psyonix's internal scale (MMR is `Mu × 20 + 100`).

Tier.description: Rank after the match (`0` unranked, `1` Bronze I … `22` Supersonic Legend).

id.description: The id of the created replay.

location.description: The replay's page on ballchasing.com (also in the `Location` header).

UploadDuplicate.description:
The replay was already uploaded. `id` and `location` point to the existing replay, except for an upload made
with a group upload token of a replay that the group's owner already has **outside** that group (and its
sub-groups): then only `error` and `chat` are set.

id.description: The id of the existing replay.

location.description: The existing replay's page on ballchasing.com.

UploadOverQuota.description: The account reached its upload quota (see the `quota` of the ping endpoint).

Rank.description: A Rocket League rank (only set for ranked playlists).

id.description: Rank code, as used by the `min-rank` and `max-rank` filters.

division.description: Division, from 1 (absent for ranks without divisions).

id.description: The id of the player on the platform.

player_number.description: Split-screen player number (absent for the main player).

pro.description: Whether the player is a known pro player.

ReplaySummary.description: A replay in a listing (no stats).

count.description:
Total number of replays matching the filters (all pages), counted up to 10,000 (more reads 10000). Absent
when no replay matches.

next.description:
Full URL of the next page, with the same filters: call it as is (with your `Authorization` header).
Absent on the last page.

ReplayBase.description: What every replay response has, whatever its processing status.

status.description:
* `ok`: processed, all the fields are set
* `pending`: not processed yet: retry later
* `failed`: the replay file could not be processed

CoreCounters.description:
Counters read as is from the replay file, counted by Rocket League itself.
**Omitted** when the replay does not track them (replays from before Rocket League's September 2026
update), `0` when it does but the value is zero.

flip_resets.description: Flip resets (as counted by the game, not verified by ballchasing).

PlayerCore.description: Core stats of a player in a replay.

mvp.description: Whether the player was the MVP.

amount_stolen.description: Boost collected in the opponent half.

amount_overfill.description: Boost wasted by collecting pads over 100.

percent_zero_boost.description: Percent of the time with no boost.

percent_full_boost.description: Percent of the time with full boost.

percent_boost_0_25.description: Percent of the time with 0-25 boost.

percent_boost_25_50.description: Percent of the time with 25-50 boost.

percent_boost_50_75.description: Percent of the time with 50-75 boost.

percent_boost_75_100.description: Percent of the time with 75-100 boost.

time_wall.description: Seconds on the walls (replays processed with repgen 4.0+).

avg_speed_percentage.description: Average speed, in percent of the max speed.

percent_slow_speed.description: Percent of the time at slow speed.

percent_boost_speed.description: Percent of the time at boost speed.

percent_supersonic_speed.description: Percent of the time at supersonic speed.

percent_ground.description: Percent of the time on the ground.

percent_low_air.description: Percent of the time in low air.

percent_high_air.description: Percent of the time in high air.

percent_wall.description: Percent of the time on the walls.

PlayerPositioning.description:
Positioning stats of a player. `avg_distance_to_mates` and the `percent_most_*`,
`percent_closest_to_ball` and `percent_farthest_from_ball` fields are only set in replay stats.

avg_distance_to_ball_possession.description: Average distance to the ball while the team has it (uu).

avg_distance_to_ball_no_possession.description: Average distance to the ball while the other team has it (uu).

time_infront_ball.description: Seconds in front of the ball.

time_most_back.description: Seconds as the most back player.

time_most_forward.description: Seconds as the most forward player.

time_closest_to_ball.description: Seconds as the closest player to the ball.

time_farthest_from_ball.description: Seconds as the farthest player from the ball.

percent_defensive_third.description: Percent of the time in the defensive third.

percent_offensive_third.description: Percent of the time in the offensive third.

percent_neutral_third.description: Percent of the time in the neutral third.

percent_defensive_half.description: Percent of the time in the defensive half.

percent_offensive_half.description: Percent of the time in the offensive half.

percent_behind_ball.description: Percent of the time behind the ball.

percent_infront_ball.description: Percent of the time in front of the ball.

percent_most_back.description: Percent of the time as the most back player.

percent_most_forward.description: Percent of the time as the most forward player.

percent_closest_to_ball.description: Percent of the time as the closest player to the ball.

percent_farthest_from_ball.description: Percent of the time as the farthest player from the ball.

Demo.description:
Demolitions. The `*_in_defensive_half` / `*_in_offensive_half` split is based on the attacker's position;
it is **omitted** for replays processed before October 2026 (until they are reprocessed).

inflicted_in_defensive_half.description: Demolitions inflicted while the attacker was in its defensive half.

inflicted_in_offensive_half.description: Demolitions inflicted while the attacker was in its offensive half.

taken_in_defensive_half.description: Demolitions taken while the attacker was in its defensive half.

taken_in_offensive_half.description: Demolitions taken while the attacker was in its offensive half.

PlayerStats.description: Stats of a player in a replay.

start_time.description: When the player joined, in seconds since the start of the replay.

end_time.description: When the player left, in seconds since the start of the replay.

time_in_side.description: Seconds the ball spent in the team side.

TeamBoost.description:
Boost stats of a team. `bpm`, `bcpm` and `avg_amount` are absent from a group's `cumulative` stats;
the `percent_*` fields are only set in group stats.

amount_stolen.description: Boost collected in the opponent half.

amount_overfill.description: Boost wasted by collecting pads over 100.

percent_zero_boost.description: Percent of the time with no boost.

percent_full_boost.description: Percent of the time with full boost.

time_wall.description: Seconds on the walls (replays processed with repgen 4.0+).

TeamPositioning.description: Positioning stats of a team (the `avg_distance_*` fields only in group stats).

time_infront_ball.description: Seconds in front of the ball.

avg_distance_to_ball_possession.description: Average distance to the ball while the team has it (uu).

avg_distance_to_ball_no_possession.description: Average distance to the ball while the other team has it (uu).

TeamStats.description: Stats of a team in a replay.

Server.description: The game server the match was played on, when the replay tells it.

Replay.title: Processed replay
Replay.description:
A processed replay with its stats.

`play_duration` is the time actually played, in seconds, without the kickoff countdowns (omitted for replays
processed before it was computed).

rocket_league_id.description: The id Rocket League gave the replay.

recorder.description: Name of the player who recorded the replay.

duration.description: Duration of the replay, in seconds.

play_duration.description: Time actually played, in seconds, without the kickoff countdowns.

season_type.description: `free2play` for the free to play seasons, absent for the old seasons.

date_has_timezone.description: Whether `date` has a real timezone (old replays only have a local time).

groups.description: The groups of the replay that you can see.

ReplayPending.title: Pending or failed replay
ReplayPending.description: A replay that is not processed (yet): only the metadata is available.

ReplayPatch.description:
Only the fields that are set are changed; all the changes are applied together, or none. An empty object changes
nothing.

group.description:
Id of the group to move the replay to (one of yours), or `""` to take it out of its group. The replay leaves
the other groups of yours it was directly in.

DailyLimitError.description: The daily limit on other people's replay files is reached.

limit.description: Files of other people the account can download per UTC day.

count.description: Distinct files of other people downloaded today.

PlayerIdentification.description:
How to identify the same player across multiple replays:

* `by-id`: by platform id
* `by-name`: by name. Some tournaments (e.g. RLCS) make players use a pool of generic Steam accounts, meaning the
  same player could end up using 2 different accounts in 2 series: that's when `by-name` comes in handy.

GroupSummary.description: A group in a listing (no stats).

direct_replays.description: Replays directly in the group that you can see.

indirect_replays.description: Replays in its sub-groups (at any depth) that you can see.

shared.description: Whether the group is shared (its replays visible to others through it, whatever their visibility).

next.description:
Full URL of the next page, with the same filters: call it as is (with your `Authorization` header).
Absent on the last page.

TeamIdentification.description:
How to identify the same team across multiple replays:

* `by-distinct-players`: teams have a fixed roster of players for every single game
* `by-player-clusters`: teams allow player rotations, or a sub can replace another player

name.description: The new group's name: 3 to 255 bytes once trimmed, unique among the groups of the same parent (of yours).

parent.description: If set, the new group is created as a child of this group (one of yours, by id).

dedup.description:
Count each game once (see "Replays of the same game" in `GET /groups/{id}`). `false`: every replay counts, like
the groups created before this setting existed.

link.description: API URL of the new group (also in the `Location` header).

GroupPlayerCore.description: Core stats of a player in a group.

GroupPlayerCumulative.description: Totals of a player over the games of the group.

GroupPlayerAverage.description: Per-game averages of a player over the games of the group.

GroupPlayerStats.description: A player of the group and its stats.

GroupTeamCumulative.description: Totals of a team over the games of the group.

GroupTeamAverage.description: Per-game averages of a team over the games of the group.

GroupTeamStats.description: A team of the group and its stats.

GroupDuplicates.description:
Replays of the same game among the group's replays you may see. The same counts whatever `dedup`: only the stats
change. Which replays they are: `GET /groups/{id}/duplicate-replays`.

duplicate_replays.description: `total_replays - unique_games`: the replays of a game already held in another replay.

Group.description:
A replay group, with the stats of its players and teams.

`players` and `teams` are only set when `status` is `ok`: until then, retry later (`pending_replays`), fix or
remove the failed replays (`failed_replays`, listed in `failed_replays` for the group's owner), or use smaller
groups (`too_many_replays`).

shared.description: Whether the group is shared (visible to others).

dedup.description:
The group's setting: count each game once (`true`) or every replay (`false`). It is the default of the
`dedup` parameter. See "Replays of the same game" above.

failed_replays.description: Ids of the replays that could not be processed (only for the group's owner).

GroupPatch.description:
Only the fields that are set are changed; all the changes are applied together, or none. An empty object changes
nothing (`204`).

parent.description:
Id of the new parent group (one of yours), or `""` to make the group a top level one. A group cannot be moved
under itself or one of its sub-groups, and trees are 32 levels deep at most.

shared.description:
Share the group (`true`) or stop sharing it (`false`). Everyone can then open the group and its sub-groups,
with all your replays in them, whatever their visibility.

dedup.description:
Count each game once (`true`) or every replay (`false`), in this group and all its sub-groups (see "Replays of
the same game" in `GET /groups/{id}`).

assign_replays.description:
Ids of replays to put directly in this group (replays you can see: yours, or other people's public and
unlisted ones). A replay leaves the other groups of yours it was directly in.

unassign_replays.description: Ids of replays to take out of your groups (whichever group of yours they are in).

list.description: One row per replay not counted when the group counts each game once, sorted by `replay_id`.

replay_id.description: A replay of a game already held in another replay of the group.

same_game_as.description: The replay that counts for that game.

next.description: Full URL of the next page, absent on the last page.

token.description: The group upload token, to send as is in the `Authorization` header of `POST /v2/upload`.

created_at.description: When the group got its first token.

updated_at.description: When the token was last replaced (absent if it never was).

generation.description: 1 for the first token, incremented each time it is replaced.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit reached. Wait `Retry-After` seconds before retrying.

BadRequest.description:
Invalid request: a bad parameter or body, or a parameter that is not valid UTF-8 or holds a NUL character.
`error` tells what is wrong.

example.error: invalid id "abc\x00": must not contain a NUL character

NotFound.description: No such resource, or you cannot see it.

PayloadTooLarge.description:
The request body is over 32 KiB (the limit of every endpoint but the upload). The body is plain text, and the
connection is closed.
